output.title: The Second Trip
output.excerpt: Picture a woman at a rent assistance office. She opens the envelope she’s been holding flat against her coat. The notice asked for her lease. She brought it. The clerk reads it and asks for last month’s rent receipt. She has that too. It’s at home. “You can come back tomorrow,” the clerk says. He…

summary: The Second Trip is an essay about how a missing line on a notice can cost someone a morning. It asks how everyday decisions can give people back their time and make essential help easier to reach.
